spectral.true_color: Dark to medium green dominates. Tan, olive-gray, and pale beige patches form irregular openings, with the clearest tan contrast in the upper center. Narrow dark bands cross parts of the scene, and a few compact pale flecks occur centrally and farther south. Confidence: high for these visual observations.
spectral.false_color: Red to crimson vegetation covers most of the patch. Pale true-color openings generally become gray-green or muted pink-gray, while much of the surrounding vegetation becomes strongly red. Some dark bands remain dark red rather than becoming clearly water-like. Confidence: high for the displayed color relationships.

implications.claim: Widespread strong red response supports substantial leafy vegetation with relatively high near-infrared reflectance.
Muted red and gray-green openings probably contain less leafy cover, more exposed substrate, or a mixture of both.
Differences in red intensity may reflect canopy density, vegetation type, illumination, or physiological condition; they do not uniquely measure vegetation health.
The upper-center pale surfaces are plausible exposed soil or rock, but their composition cannot be distinguished.
No unambiguous open-water body is visible, so water turbidity cannot be assessed.
Dark vegetation and terrain shading cannot establish soil or canopy moisture differences from these renderings.
The small bright patches could include rock, soil, or built material; their colors do not establish buildings or pavement.

spectral.not_revealed: These display renderings do not provide quantitative reflectance, reliable vegetation indices, canopy height, species, crop identity, soil composition, water content, or change through time. They also cannot uniquely separate physiological stress from sparse cover and illumination effects. Confidence: high.

summaries.w25: Probably wooded terrain contains irregular sparse-cover openings, especially centrally and northward (medium confidence). Strong red false-color response indicates extensive leafy vegetation (high confidence).
summaries.w50: The patch is probably predominantly wooded, with irregular openings concentrated in the upper center and central-to-eastern areas (medium confidence). Strong false-color red indicates extensive leafy vegetation (high confidence). Pale patches likely mix sparse cover and exposed substrate; their origin and any management remain uncertain (low confidence).
summaries.w100: This 1.2 km patch probably contains predominantly woody vegetation, with estimated cover of 68% dense vegetation, 25% sparse or mixed cover, and 7% exposed substrate (medium confidence overall). Irregular openings cluster in the upper center and central-to-eastern areas; the southwest is more continuously vegetated (high confidence). Strong red false-color response supports extensive leafy cover (high confidence). Curving boundaries and dark diagonal belts suggest terrain influence (medium confidence). A possible central track is uncertain (low confidence). No clear water body or substantial settlement is evident (medium confidence); biome, season, and active land-management processes remain unresolved.
summaries.w200:
The patch is probably a predominantly wooded landscape with irregular open areas (medium confidence). Visual cover estimates are 68% dense vegetation, 25% sparse vegetation mixed with exposed ground, and 7% predominantly bare substrate; the sparse-versus-bare distinction is uncertain (medium confidence overall).

A lobed pale opening with vegetated islands occupies the upper center. Additional branching openings occur centrally and along the eastern side, while the lower-left area is more continuously vegetated (high confidence). Dark southwest–northeast belts and curved boundaries suggest uneven terrain, although canopy density and shading are confounded (medium confidence).

Strong red false-color response indicates widespread leafy vegetation, while muted gray-green openings imply reduced leafy cover or greater substrate exposure (high and medium confidence, respectively). These colors do not independently establish vegetation health or moisture (high confidence).

A narrow central pale trace could be a track, and a small eastern bright patch could be soil, rock, or built material (low confidence). No clear open-water body or substantial settlement is evident (medium confidence). Natural openings and managed clearings remain difficult to distinguish. Crop types, forestry practices, active erosion, flooding, season, and a specific biome cannot be established from this single paired rendering (high confidence).
summaries.w400:
This 1.2 × 1.2 km patch is probably predominantly wooded, with irregular sparse-cover and exposed-ground openings (medium confidence). Approximate visual fractions are 68% dense vegetation, 25% sparse vegetation mixed with substrate, and 7% predominantly exposed soil or rock. The overall division is tentative, particularly between sparse vegetation and bare ground (medium confidence).

The most distinctive pale opening lies in the upper center and extends slightly into the upper-left cell. It is lobed, contains darker vegetated islands, and measures roughly 300–350 m wide by 350–420 m long (medium confidence in dimensions). Central and eastern cells contain additional branching or elongated openings, separated by dark vegetated strips. The lower-left portion is more continuously vegetated, whereas small pale patches persist across the lower center and southeastern edge (high confidence in spatial pattern).

Broad dark belts trend approximately southwest–northeast through portions of the patch. Along with curved cover boundaries, they suggest terrain-related organization or shading, but denser canopy could contribute to the same appearance (medium confidence). A discontinuous pale trace in the center may be an access track or simply an exposed terrain edge (low confidence). A compact bright patch near the lower part of the middle-right cell is visible, but its material is unresolved (high confidence in visibility; low confidence in classification).

True color is dominated by dark and medium greens, interrupted by tan and olive-gray surfaces. False color shows extensive strong red vegetation, with muted red or gray-green openings (high confidence). This supports substantial leafy cover and locally reduced vegetation density or greater substrate exposure (high and medium confidence, respectively). Red intensity alone cannot isolate physiological vigor, moisture, species, or canopy structure (high confidence).

No unambiguous open-water body, substantial settlement, or organized crop-field pattern is apparent (medium confidence). The openings could be natural rocky areas, managed clearings, or a mixture (low confidence). Recent harvest, irrigation, erosion, flooding, and clearing are not demonstrated; their timing would require additional evidence (high confidence). A specific biome, climate, or season remains unresolved. At 10 m, mixed pixels and display interpolation limit interpretation of narrow tracks, small structures, channels, and precise boundaries (high confidence).
